- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after recent spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or shows strong downward momentum, model often underestimates; increase forecast slightly to counteract mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model frequently overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply downward correction of 1–3% to avoid overreaction.
- When sentiment flips from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags in adjusting; delay or dampen forecast change until sentiment stabilizes.
- If model forecast is >10% above recent 7-day average, consider mean reversion bias — reduce forecast toward historical range, especially if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates early in the period (first 5–7 days) — apply a 1–2% downward bias to first 5 days if sentiment is neutral or mixed.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” (neutral) or “-1.00” (negative) in last 3–5 days, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% to align with downward trend reversal.
